newsitem.title: FRANCE: French give left "new chance", rebuff Chirac - press.
newsitem.headline: French give left "new chance", rebuff Chirac - press.

text.p: French media said on Monday the election of the Socialist-led opposition was a new chance for the left and a stinging punishment for President Jacques Chirac and his centre-right allies.
But many expressed concern that voters did not know what they wanted for France, voting for one side in one election and the other in the next.

"The new chance," the left-leaning daily Liberation said in a front-page headline after the Socialist-led opposition won a majority in the 577-seat National Assembly just four years after voters dumped the left in a right-wing landslide.
"The punishment," the daily France-Soir said in a banner headline targeting the right.
"Lionel Jospin's great revenge," the Parisien said, referring to Jospin's defeat in the runoff for the presidency against conservative Jacques Chirac two years ago.
"Jospin on his way to the prime minister's office," the conservative daily Le Figaro said, saying it was a "severe defeat" for the outgoing right-wing government and a "lost gamble" for Chirac.

It said Chirac had weakened himself by calling the vote early, wrongly believing voters would elect the centre-right for five more years. He will have to work in a hostile tandem with Jospin at the head of a left-wing government.
But it underlined an opinion poll showing that 61 percent of French people wanted Chirac to stay on.

"What a thrashing! What a beautiful thrashing!" exulted the Communist daily L'Humanite. "Last Sunday voters inflicted a severe correction to the right, yesterday they pronounced the definitive verdict: it's a punishment!"
Serge July, publisher of Liberation, said Jospin's victory was one of modesty compared to the high-handedness of the government, adding that the centre-right had led one of the worst campaigns ever.
Chirac called the election 10 months early, saying that France needed a "new elan" to help it qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
Le Figaro showed a ballot box labelled "left" crashing through the roof of the Elysee palace with an aide saying "Yes, Mr President, the results have just come in".
Writer Jean d'Ormesson, of the French Academy, said in Le Figaro that "the French tried the right. And then the left. And then the right again. And then the left again."
"They are like poor birds banging their heads against a window, like brainless sheep vainly seeking an exit. Once again, I doubt that they have knocked at the right door," he wrote.
